questionText: Why is statelessness the most important REST constraint for scalability?

target.learningOutcome: The learner can explain how self-contained requests simplify routing and failover while distinguishing session context from stored resource state.

claims.statement: A REST request contains the information needed to understand it independently of earlier requests, so connectors do not retain application state between requests.
Stateless interaction improves visibility, reliability, and scalability but can repeat per-request data and move more application-state responsibility to the client.

examples.title: Create a long-running export and read it from any API instance

validation.expected: The later GET contains a resource identifier and credential instead of relying on an instance session

visuals.title: Allowed resource state compared with hidden session context

notes: The answer directly rejects the common misconception that stateless REST requires JWT or forbids server-side business data.
